detail.longDescription: I have an application that can be included at any point in a person's page - e.g. half-way down the page after their own HTML has been output. My application shows database information. It saves this information back (when somebody submits the edit form) by POSTing back to the same page. The POST is then caught by my app and the data is saved to a DB. I would then like to redirect back to the same page (because that's how I've done form submissions for years - if the user wants, they can refresh the page and they won't see a "reconfirm post" message). But because this app can be included half-way down the user's page I can't do a traditional HTTP redirect, it has to be a JavaScript redirect. <script>window.location.href = '/foo.html?jkl#bar';</script> But it's not redirecting when I add an anchor. Is this sort of redirect with the anchor prohibited? If I remove the anchor it works fine (but obviously doesn't go to where the anchor is in the page).
